name: Constant-step two-step Adams–Bashforth ODE integration
definition: For y′=f(t,y), t_n=t_0+nh, h>0, let F_n=f(t_n,y_n). For n≥1 set y_(n+1)=y_n+h(3F_n−F_(n−1))/2. On y′=λy with z=hλ the characteristic equation is r²−(1+3z/2)r+z/2=0.
variables: h constant positive step; t_n grid time; y_n state; F_n stored slope; λ scalar linear test rate; r characteristic root
assumptions: Locally Lipschitz dynamics, sufficiently smooth solution with bounded derivatives through order three on a finite interval, and starting states accurate to O(h²) on a uniform grid
limitations: Second-order method; explicit stability restrictions apply, including negative-real scalar test interval −1≤z≤0; not a general stiff solver or a variable-step formula
failure_conditions: Missing or inconsistent starting pair or changed step spacing
Nonfinite state or derivative, or unresolved stability restriction
computation: Obtain y_1 with a sufficiently accurate one-step integrator, for example one forward Euler step from exact y_0 has O(h²) state error. Cache F_0 and F_1, compute each new state with the stated recurrence, evaluate its derivative and shift the two stored slopes. Reject invalid grid or nonfinite results; choose steps using problem-dependent accuracy and stability requirements.

source.citation: LeMesurier, B., Numerical Methods and Analysis with Julia (draft), §6.8, Eq. (6.11), https://lemesurierb.people.charleston.edu/numerical-methods-and-analysis-julia/docs/ODE-IVP-7-multi-step-methods-Adams-Bashforth.html ; characteristic polynomial and real-axis interval independently derived.

required_inputs: ODE, initial values or starting procedure, constant step and solve budget
mechanism_note: Integrates a linear extrapolation of two previous slopes; unlike forward Euler, it retains history, and unlike BDF2 it requires no implicit solve. At z=0 the roots are 0 and 1; the local exact-state defect is 5h³y‴(t_n)/12+O(h⁴) with the additional derivative regularity.

name: Constant-step two-step Adams–Moulton ODE integration
definition: For y′=f(t,y), t_n=t_0+nh, h>0, let F_n=f(t_n,y_n). Solve y_(n+1)=y_n+h(5f(t_(n+1),y_(n+1))+8F_n−F_(n−1))/12. On y′=λy with z=hλ the characteristic equation is (1−5z/12)r²−(1+8z/12)r+z/12=0.
variables: h constant positive step; t_n grid time; y_n state; F_n stored slope; λ scalar linear test rate; r characteristic root
assumptions: Locally Lipschitz dynamics, solution derivatives bounded through order four on a finite interval, starting states accurate to O(h³), and sufficiently accurate locally consistent implicit solves on a uniform grid
limitations: Third-order constant-step method, not A-stable; negative-real scalar test interval −6≤z≤0. Implicit solves, startup and history are required; residual alone is not an error certificate
failure_conditions: Missing or inconsistent starting pair or changed spacing
Nonfinite state or unresolved implicit solve, scaled residual or stability restriction
computation: Obtain y_1 using a sufficiently accurate one-step starter, for example RK4. Store the last two slopes; optionally use AB2 as an initial guess only. Solve R(v)=v−y_n−h(5f(t_(n+1),v)+8F_n−F_(n−1))/12=0 with a declared tolerance and finite solve budget on the locally consistent branch. Require O(h⁴) or smaller per-step state solve error for third-order analysis. Reject unresolved solves; a single predictor substitution is not the same implicit method.

source.citation: University of Bielefeld, Computational Physics SoSe 2026, Multi-Step Methods, Adams–Moulton table order 3 and implicit equation discussion, https://roesner.pages.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/lectures/computational-physics/semester/sose2026/lecture/07_ode/05_multistep_methods.html ; moments and characteristic polynomial independently derived.

required_inputs: ODE right-hand side, starting pair, constant step and nonlinear solve policy
mechanism_note: Quadratic slope interpolation through one future and two past/current grid nodes generalizes the implicit trapezoidal rule; conservatively counted as a variant. At z=0 the characteristic roots are 0 and 1; the local exact-state defect is −h⁴y⁽⁴⁾(t_n)/24+O(h⁵) with additional derivative regularity.
